# Brief H4: Montagent square ad

**15 seconds · 1080×1080 · 30 fps · 1:1.** Deliver one MP4 with sound.

A square ad for Montagent to run in social feeds, where most people scroll past with the
sound off. In fifteen seconds it has to make one claim and back it up: your agent edits
video the way it edits code, and here is a real session proving it. The viewer should come
away knowing what Montagent is, having seen the real product at work, and with the brand in
their head. It should feel like a confident product ad, not a tutorial or a screen
recording with a logo stuck on.

Everything you need is in the asset pack; its `README.md` lists it. Use the pack's fonts
and brand colours. The proof is `screen/session.mp4` (a real 55-second session, far longer
than the ad, so choose what to show) and the two stills in `stills/`. The music is
`music/bed-120bpm.wav` at 120 BPM. The brand is in `brand/`.

How the piece is structured, how long each part runs, how things enter and leave, and how
the square frame is composed are yours to decide. What follows is what it must deliver.

## What it must deliver

| Beat | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Hook | Within the first three seconds, on-screen words tell the viewer that this is about an AI agent editing video. The viewer should not need sound to get it. |
| Proof | The real product is shown at work: footage from `screen/session.mp4` and/or `stills/session-01.png`, framed so the terminal reads as a terminal in a square frame, not as a tiny letterboxed strip. |
| Result | The viewer sees what the session produced: `stills/session-02.png`, the rendered video with its new subtitle. It must be clear that this picture is the outcome of the work just shown. |
| Claim | One short line of on-screen copy, in your words, says why this matters (for example that the video is a file the agent can read, check and change). One word or one shape in it may carry the accent colour. |
| Brand | The piece ends on the Montagent mark, wordmark or lockup, on a brand ground, held long enough to read. |
| Sound | The music bed runs under the whole piece and ends cleanly with the picture. |

## Acceptance checklist

**Hook**
- [ ] On-screen text in the first three seconds says the piece is about an agent editing video, and is readable at phone size.

**Proof**
- [ ] Footage or a still of the real terminal session is on screen, large enough that the frame reads as a working terminal.
- [ ] Nothing from the session is stretched or squashed; any crop to the square frame is deliberate and keeps the interesting part (the edit, the diff) in view.

**Result**
- [ ] `stills/session-02.png` appears after the proof and is clearly presented as its outcome.
- [ ] Its subtitle ("Hello, Montagent" and the line beneath) is legible in the delivered frame.

**Claim**
- [ ] One line of copy states the benefit in plain words, is on screen long enough to read twice, and contains no spelling errors.
- [ ] The accent colour is used on at most one word or one shape at a time, never a whole line of text.

**Brand**
- [ ] The final shot is the brand (mark, wordmark or lockup), legible and undistorted, on screen for at least the last second and a half.
- [ ] Brand colours and the Inter faces are used throughout; no other typefaces or off-palette colours.

**Whole piece**
- [ ] Cuts and major entrances sit on the music's beats.
- [ ] The music is audible from the first frame and has ended or faded to silence by 15 s; nothing is cut off abruptly.
- [ ] No text overflows the frame or collides with other elements; nothing sits in the outer 5% of the frame.
- [ ] No corner labels, watermarks, timecodes, placeholder text or frame chrome anywhere.
